speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यदहंकारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे ।
मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति ॥
iast:
yadahaṃkāramāśritya na yotsya iti manyase |
mithyaiṣa vyavasāyaste prakṛtistvāṃ niyokṣyati ||
english: If, relying on ego, you think 'I will not fight', that resolve of yours is in vain: your own nature will compel you.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा ।
कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत् ॥
iast:
svabhāvajena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā |
kartuṃ necchasi yanmohātkariṣyasyavaśo'pi tat ||
english: Bound by your own action, born of your nature, son of Kunti, what you do not wish to do out of delusion you will do, even against your will.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति ।
भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥
iast:
īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛddeśe'rjuna tiṣṭhati |
bhrāmayansarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā ||
english: The Lord dwells in the heart of all beings, Arjuna, making all beings turn by his power, as if they were mounted on a machine.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत ।
तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥
iast:
tameva śaraṇaṃ gaccha sarvabhāvena bhārata |
tatprasādātparāṃ śāntiṃ sthānaṃ prāpsyasi śāśvatam ||
english: Take refuge in him alone with your whole being, Arjuna; by his grace you will reach supreme peace and the eternal abode.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्‌गुह्यतरं मया ।
विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
iast:
iti te jñānamākhyātaṃ guhyādguhyataraṃ mayā |
vimṛśyaitadaśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru ||
english: Thus I have taught you wisdom more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you choose.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥
iast:
sarvaguhyatamaṃ bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ |
iṣṭo'si me dṛḍhamiti tato vakṣyāmi te hitam ||
english: Hear once more my supreme word, the most secret of all. You are dearly loved by me, so I will tell you what is for your good.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।
मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥
iast:
manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru |
māmevaiṣyasi satyaṃ te pratijāne priyo'si me ||
english: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, worship me, bow down to me. You will come to me; I promise you truly, for you are dear to me.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज ।
अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥
iast:
sarvadharmānparityajya māmekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja |
ahaṃ tvāṃ sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ ||
english: Let go of all dharmas and take refuge in me alone. I will free you from all sins; do not grieve.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन ।
न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति ॥
iast:
idaṃ te nātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadācana |
na cāśuśrūṣave vācyaṃ na ca māṃ yo'bhyasūyati ||
english: This is never to be told by you to one without austerity, or without devotion, or to one unwilling to listen, or to one who finds fault with me.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
य इमं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति ।
भक्तिं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः ॥
iast:
ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ madbhakteṣvabhidhāsyati |
bhaktiṃ mayi parāṃ kṛtvā māmevaiṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ ||
english: One who teaches this supreme secret to my devotees, having shown the highest devotion to me, will without doubt come to me.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्चिन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः ।
भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि ॥
iast:
na ca tasmānmanuṣyeṣu kaścinme priyakṛttamaḥ |
bhavitā na ca me tasmādanyaḥ priyataro bhuvi ||
english: No one among people does more to please me than they do, and no one on earth will ever be dearer to me than they are.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः ।
ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः ॥
iast:
adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādamāvayoḥ |
jñānayajñena tenāhamiṣṭaḥ syāmiti me matiḥ ||
english: And whoever studies this sacred dialogue of ours, by them I would be worshipped through the sacrifice of knowledge: that is my view.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च शृणुयादपि यो नरः ।
सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभाँल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥
iast:
śraddhāvānanasūyaśca śṛṇuyādapi yo naraḥ |
so'pi muktaḥ śubhām̐llokānprāpnuyātpuṇyakarmaṇām ||
english: And the person who simply listens, with faith and without finding fault, they too, freed, will reach the auspicious worlds of those who do good deeds.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा ।
कच्चिदज्ञानसंमोहः प्रनष्टस्ते धनंजय ॥
iast:
kaccidetacchrutaṃ pārtha tvayaikāgreṇa cetasā |
kaccidajñānasaṃmohaḥ pranaṣṭaste dhanaṃjaya ||
english: Have you heard this with an attentive mind, son of Pritha? Has your confusion born of ignorance been destroyed, Arjuna?

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
नष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत ।
स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥
iast:
naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtirlabdhā tvatprasādānmayācyuta |
sthito'smi gatasandehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava ||
english: My delusion is gone, Krishna; by your grace I have regained clear understanding. I stand firm, my doubts gone. I will do as you say.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
इत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः ।
संवादमिममश्रौषमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम् ॥
iast:
ityahaṃ vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ |
saṃvādamimamaśrauṣamadbhutaṃ romaharṣaṇam ||
english: Thus I have heard this wondrous dialogue between Krishna and the great-souled son of Pritha, which makes my hair stand on end.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
व्यासप्रसादाच्छ्रुतवानेतद्गुह्यमहं परम् ।
योगं योगेश्वरात्कृष्णात्साक्षात्कथयतः स्वयम् ॥
iast:
vyāsaprasādācchrutavānetadguhyamahaṃ param |
yogaṃ yogeśvarātkṛṣṇātsākṣātkathayataḥ svayam ||
english: By the grace of Vyasa I heard this supreme secret, this yoga, from Krishna, the lord of yoga, himself, as he spoke it directly.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम् ।
केशवार्जुनयोः पुण्यं हृष्यामि च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
iast:
rājansaṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya saṃvādamimamadbhutam |
keśavārjunayoḥ puṇyaṃ hṛṣyāmi ca muhurmuhuḥ ||
english: O king, as I recall again and again this wondrous and holy dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः ।
विस्मयो मे महान् राजन्हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः ॥
iast:
tacca saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya rūpamatyadbhutaṃ hareḥ |
vismayo me mahān rājanhṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
english: And as I recall again and again that most wondrous form of Krishna, great is my amazement, O king, and I rejoice again and again.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः ।
तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥
iast:
yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ |
tatra śrīrvijayo bhūtirdhruvā nītirmatirmama ||
english: Wherever there is Krishna, the lord of yoga, and wherever there is the son of Pritha, the archer, there are fortune, victory, prosperity and lasting good policy: that is my conviction.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
ॐ ईशा वास्यमिदँ सर्वं यत्किञ्च जगत्यां जगत् ।
तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम् ॥
iast:
oṃ īśā vāsyamidam̐ sarvaṃ yatkiñca jagatyāṃ jagat |
tena tyaktena bhuñjīthā mā gṛdhaḥ kasyasviddhanam ||
english: Om. All this, whatever moves in this moving world, is to be clothed by the Lord. Through that renunciation, enjoy; do not covet anyone's wealth.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतँ समाः ।
एवं त्वयि नान्यथेतोऽस्ति न कर्म लिप्यते नरे ॥
iast:
kurvanneveha karmāṇi jijīviṣecchatam̐ samāḥ |
evaṃ tvayi nānyatheto'sti na karma lipyate nare ||
english: Doing works here, one should wish to live a hundred years. For you who live this way there is no other path than this: action does not cling to such a person.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
असुर्या नाम ते लोका अन्धेन तमसाऽऽवृताः ।
ताँस्ते प्रेत्याभिगच्छन्ति ये के चात्महनो जनाः ॥
iast:
asuryā nāma te lokā andhena tamasā''vṛtāḥ |
tām̐ste pretyābhigacchanti ye ke cātmahano janāḥ ||
english: Those worlds called demonic are covered in blind darkness. To them, after death, go all those people who slay the self.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
अनेजदेकं मनसो जवीयो नैनद्देवा आप्नुवन्पूर्वमर्षत् ।
तद्धावतोऽन्यानत्येति तिष्ठत्तस्मिन्नपो मातरिश्वा दधाति ॥
iast:
anejadekaṃ manaso javīyo nainaddevā āpnuvanpūrvamarṣat |
taddhāvato'nyānatyeti tiṣṭhattasminnapo mātariśvā dadhāti ||
english: Unmoving, the One is swifter than the mind; the gods could not reach it, for it had gone ahead. Standing still, it outruns all who run. In it, Matarishvan, the wind, sets the waters in place.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
तदेजति तन्नैजति तद्दूरे तद्वन्तिके ।
तदन्तरस्य सर्वस्य तदु सर्वस्यास्य बाह्यतः ॥
iast:
tadejati tannaijati taddūre tadvantike |
tadantarasya sarvasya tadu sarvasyāsya bāhyataḥ ||
english: It moves; it does not move. It is far, and it is near. It is within all this, and it is outside all this.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
यस्तु सर्वाणि भूतान्यात्मन्येवानुपश्यति ।
सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं ततो न विजुगुप्सते ॥
iast:
yastu sarvāṇi bhūtānyātmanyevānupaśyati |
sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ tato na vijugupsate ||
english: Whoever sees all beings in the Self, and the Self in all beings, no longer feels aversion to anyone.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
यस्मिन्सर्वाणि भूतान्यात्मैवाभूद्विजानतः ।
तत्र को मोहः कः शोक एकत्वमनुपश्यतः ॥
iast:
yasminsarvāṇi bhūtānyātmaivābhūdvijānataḥ |
tatra ko mohaḥ kaḥ śoka ekatvamanupaśyataḥ ||
english: When, for one who knows, all beings have become the Self, what delusion, what grief can there be for one who sees oneness?

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
स पर्यगाच्छुक्रमकायमव्रण-मस्नाविरँ शुद्धमपापविद्धम् ।
कविर्मनीषी परिभूः स्वयम्भू-र्याथातथ्यतोऽर्थान् व्यदधाच्छाश्वतीभ्यः समाभ्यः ॥
iast:
sa paryagācchukramakāyamavraṇa-masnāviram̐ śuddhamapāpaviddham |
kavirmanīṣī paribhūḥ svayambhū-ryāthātathyato'rthān vyadadhācchāśvatībhyaḥ samābhyaḥ ||
english: He has gone everywhere: bright, bodiless, without wound, without sinews, pure, untouched by evil. The seer, the wise one, all-encompassing, self-existent, he has set all things rightly in order through endless years.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
अन्धं तमः प्रविशन्ति येऽविद्यामुपासते ।
ततो भूय इव ते तमो य उ विद्यायाँ रताः ॥
iast:
andhaṃ tamaḥ praviśanti ye'vidyāmupāsate |
tato bhūya iva te tamo ya u vidyāyām̐ ratāḥ ||
english: Into blind darkness enter those who worship ignorance; into a darkness even greater, as it were, enter those who delight in knowledge.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
अन्यदेवाहुर्विद्ययाऽन्यदाहुरविद्यया ।
इति शुश्रुम धीराणां ये नस्तद्विचचक्षिरे ॥
iast:
anyadevāhurvidyayā'nyadāhuravidyayā |
iti śuśruma dhīrāṇāṃ ye nastadvicacakṣire ||
english: One thing, they say, comes from knowledge; another, they say, from ignorance. So we have heard from the wise who explained it to us.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
विद्यां चाविद्यां च यस्तद्वेदोभयँ सह ।
अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते ॥
iast:
vidyāṃ cāvidyāṃ ca yastadvedobhayam̐ saha |
avidyayā mṛtyuṃ tīrtvā vidyayā'mṛtamaśnute ||
english: Whoever knows both knowledge and ignorance together crosses death through ignorance and attains immortality through knowledge.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
अन्धं तमः प्रविशन्ति येऽसम्भूतिमुपासते ।
ततो भूय इव ते तमो य उ सम्भूत्याँ रताः ॥
iast:
andhaṃ tamaḥ praviśanti ye'sambhūtimupāsate |
tato bhūya iva te tamo ya u sambhūtyām̐ ratāḥ ||
english: Into blind darkness enter those who worship non-becoming; into a darkness even greater, as it were, enter those who delight in becoming.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
अन्यदेवाहुः सम्भवादन्यदाहुरसम्भवात् ।
इति शुश्रुम धीराणां ये नस्तद्विचचक्षिरे ॥
iast:
anyadevāhuḥ sambhavādanyadāhurasambhavāt |
iti śuśruma dhīrāṇāṃ ye nastadvicacakṣire ||
english: One thing, they say, comes from becoming; another, they say, from non-becoming. So we have heard from the wise who explained it to us.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
सम्भूतिं च विनाशं च यस्तद्वेदोभयँ सह ।
विनाशेन मृत्युं तीर्त्वा सम्भूत्याऽमृतमश्नुते ॥
iast:
sambhūtiṃ ca vināśaṃ ca yastadvedobhayam̐ saha |
vināśena mṛtyuṃ tīrtvā sambhūtyā'mṛtamaśnute ||
english: Whoever knows both becoming and destruction together crosses death through destruction and attains immortality through becoming.

speaker: seeker
devanagari:
हिरण्मयेन पात्रेण सत्यस्यापिहितं मुखम् ।
तत्त्वं पूषन्नपावृणु सत्यधर्माय दृष्टये ॥
iast:
hiraṇmayena pātreṇa satyasyāpihitaṃ mukham |
tattvaṃ pūṣannapāvṛṇu satyadharmāya dṛṣṭaye ||
english: The face of truth is covered by a golden vessel. Uncover it, O Pushan, so that I, devoted to truth, may see.

speaker: seeker
devanagari:
पूषन्नेकर्षे यम सूर्य प्राजापत्य व्यूह रश्मीन् समूह तेजः ।
यत्ते रूपं कल्याणतमं तत्ते पश्यामि योऽसावसौ पुरुषः सोऽहमस्मि ॥
iast:
pūṣannekarṣe yama sūrya prājāpatya vyūha raśmīn samūha tejaḥ |
yatte rūpaṃ kalyāṇatamaṃ tatte paśyāmi yo'sāvasau puruṣaḥ so'hamasmi ||
english: O Pushan, sole seer, Yama, Surya, child of Prajapati, spread apart your rays and gather in your light. That form of yours which is most blessed, I see. That person over there, I am he.

speaker: seeker
devanagari:
वायुरनिलममृतमथेदं भस्मांतँ शरीरम् ।
ॐ क्रतो स्मर कृतँ स्मर क्रतो स्मर कृतँ स्मर ॥
iast:
vāyuranilamamṛtamathedaṃ bhasmāṃtam̐ śarīram |
oṃ krato smara kṛtam̐ smara krato smara kṛtam̐ smara ||
english: Now let my breath go to the immortal wind, and let this body end in ashes. Om. O mind, remember! Remember what was done! O mind, remember! Remember what was done!

speaker: seeker
devanagari:
अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान् विश्वानि देव वयुनानि विद्वान् ।
युयोध्यस्मज्जुहुराणमेनो भूयिष्ठां ते नमउक्तिं विधेम ॥
iast:
agne naya supathā rāye asmān viśvāni deva vayunāni vidvān |
yuyodhyasmajjuhurāṇameno bhūyiṣṭhāṃ te namauktiṃ vidhema ||
english: O Agni, god who knows all our ways, lead us by the good path to prosperity. Keep far from us the sin that leads astray. We offer you our fullest words of homage.

speaker: student
devanagari:
ॐ केनेषितं पतति प्रेषितं मनः
केन प्राणः प्रथमः प्रैति युक्तः ।
केनेषितां वाचमिमां वदन्ति
चक्षुः श्रोत्रं क उ देवो युनक्ति ॥
iast:
oṃ keneṣitaṃ patati preṣitaṃ manaḥ
kena prāṇaḥ prathamaḥ praiti yuktaḥ |
keneṣitāṃ vācamimāṃ vadanti
cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ ka u devo yunakti ||
english: Om. Willed by whom, sent by whom, does the mind fly out? Yoked by whom does the first breath go forth? Willed by whom do people speak this speech? What god yokes the eye and the ear?

speaker: teacher
devanagari:
श्रोत्रस्य श्रोत्रं मनसो मनो यद्वाचो ह वाचं
स उ प्राणस्य प्राणः चक्षुषश्चक्षुः ।
अतिमुच्य धीराः प्रेत्यास्माल्लोकादमृता भवन्ति ॥
iast:
śrotrasya śrotraṃ manaso mano yadvāco ha vācaṃ
sa u prāṇasya prāṇaḥ cakṣuṣaścakṣuḥ |
atimucya dhīrāḥ pretyāsmāllokādamṛtā bhavanti ||
english: It is the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind, the speech of speech; it is the breath of breath and the eye of the eye. Letting go, the wise, departing from this world, become immortal.
